scenes.heading: INT. APARTMENT - DAY
content: The front door. Sandals thrown about around a dirty welcome mat. Next to the door, a window--shades drawn, light bleeding through the cracks.
A figure walks past the window. Three knocks. No response.
BRICK(30s, blonde) stumbles into view, shorts around his ankles. He hobbles towards the door, tugs his basketball shorts up to his waist.
Brick wears a Miami Dolphins Tagovialoa jersey, his long blonde hair tied into a bun, a couple days unwashed.
He opens the door. JERRY LEFTON(30s) stands there--unwashed jacket, with slacks, tie and shoes to match. Everyting coordinates. Nothing's clean.
Brick shields his eyes from the sunlight.
It's Jerry Lefton, I don't know if you remember. From high school?
Brick rubs his eyes and leans forward to get a better look.
Holy shit! Jerry? Shit, what's going on dude?
Goddamn! Sorry, I just- It's been forever dude! What're doing here?
Um, actually if it's okay, I just wanted to catch up, ask a few questions actually-
Oh, yeah totally. Uh-ah shit where are my manners man?
Oh, really? We can talk here-I can be quick if you're.
Nah, totally! I insist man...God knows I could use the company.
Brick looks Jerry up and down. Then waves him inside.
Jerry steps inside. The door closes behind him.
Jerry chops his feet on the welcome mat, he ends up just kicking more dirt lose. It reads: WELCOME TO THE MAN CAVE.
Brick is already in the kitchen, connected to the living room to the left of Jerry.
Lemme get you a cold one!
Ah cmon man. I'm gonna get you one anyways.
No really, thanks for the offer though.
Brick grabs a beer from the fridge. He moves into the living room.
Couch, loveseat, coffee table--all facing a TV propped up against a wall. Above it: Playboy centerfolds, carefully arranged, all nude.
The coffee table is scattered with dirty napkins and empty beer cans.
Take a seat dude. Make yourself at home.
Brick plops down in the loveseat. Dust billows up around him.
See you lookin' at my girls. Like 'em?
Sorry? Oh, you mean, uh- yeah.
I see ya sneaking a peek, Hah! Don't worry I put em up there for a reason.
Brick cracks open his beer can. Jerry grabs something from his pocket.
Just admiring your place, it's-uh-nice you could find somewhere. It, uh, looks... Good.
You really think so? I was going for that, you know, man cave vibe, that real party feel. No boring shit you feel me? I want that nostalgic feel.
Yeah like those good old days when we could go do shit and not worry bout anything. You remember the junior year thing at uh... Raymond's place, you remember Raymond?
I see him on Instagram sometimes-
That crazy ass party, going for that vibe completely. 24-7 non stop crazy shit.
Jerry's brow furrows. He looks up, thinking.
You mean the party where Mason's older brother got caught doing coke off of some Freshman's naked... nevermind. I thought the police showed up and everything?
Oh. Well, not those parts, don't really remember that too well, heh.
Jerry holds the object from his pocket in front of him, a BADGE. Brick takes a swig.
So, uh... God! Where are my manners, shit I'm being a shitty host right now. How you've been doing, what brings you 'round the ole stomping grounds.
Oh it's fine, actually how I've been is the reason I'm here.
Jerry shows his badge to Brick
I've been working for the city police department.
Brick stares towards the kitchen. Beyond Jerry, slightly blurred: a tall glass bong, pill bottles scattered around, white residue.
Jerry pockets his badge. Watches Brick. Follows his line of sight to the bong.
Oh no Brick. I'm criminal investigations, like a detective.
Listen Brick, I'm not here for drugs or anything like that. I just need some info on someone you were seen with recently.
Well, I don't hang around-I try not to hang around, you know, those type of people. I know I party hard man but that's not-
Can I try asking? Can't hurt, right?
Okay... I'm just a little hungover, so my mind, you know? I might not, uh-
Well let's try. Dmitri Onglestov, ring any bells? Bald, european? He hangs out at clubs around town.
Uhh, I think- yeah there was a guy like that, I'm not really-
My friend invited me to a club.
From school, what's her name. With the ass.
Everyone at our school had an ass. Surely you remember her-
I don't remember her fuckin last name man. You should be happy I remembered the initial.
That's alright Brick. Wait, Amanda with the Brown scholarship?
Oh yeah man. You should see her now. When I saw her movin' in the club, I couldn't believe.
2B, oh you haven't been, hah, just what we call it, the Black Bazaar.
Um, just Amanda. Yeah me and her got real close you know?
Jerry reaches back in his pocket.
God you should see the way she's grown-ooohwee.
Nope just me and ma girl. Lemme tell ya, she dances like a goddamn fox dude. -Ay, don't get jealous but, uh, your boy got to hit first so-

Jerry places a pile of photos on the coffee table. He fans them out like cards: Brick in the club with a scantily clad girl. Brick doing a beer bong. Security cam shot--Brick in a bathroom. A bald European man doing a line off of Brick's naked ass.
Brick, again, I'm not here for you, I'm just asking for honest answers, okay?
Did Amanda or anyone else give you a contact or a number?
You know what uhh-Hey wait what is the guy in trouble for even, can't just give away his number for nothing, I didn't even know he-
Kidnapping, possible homicide. Now: contact, number, anything?
Brick stiffens up. His movements are now robotic. He sets down his beer.
I have a card-he gave me a card.
Actually, yeah. Let me get it, it's-uh in the kitchen. You know what? I need another beer anyway, needa refill?
I don't have a- I don't drink.
How could I forget! Hahaha. Let me get that for you.
Yeah, no problem Brick. This is a huge help to me.
Brick gets up and walks into the kitchen.
HOLD ON JERRY in the foreground, gathers the photos, knocks over a couple of beer cans.
Behind him, Brick speed-walks to the fridge. Peeks inside.
Jerry bends over in his seat, picks up the cans.
Behind him, Brick glances over the fridge door - then scurries down a hallway. Out of sight.
Empty kitchen behind, Jerry sits back up. Sets the cans on the table. Slides the photos into his pocket.
One of the cans has condensation. Still cold. He picks it up, shakes it - 3/4 full.
Jerry's eyes snap toward the empty kitchen.
He pops out of his seat. Gun already in hand.
Jerry sweeps the room. Two hands on his pistol, raised. One foot after the other.
His shoulder bumps the fridge door shut.
He takes cover at the hallway entrance.
The hallway stretches ahead. At the end: a door that hangs ajar. Light bleeds through the crack.
Jerry swings around the corner, gun aimed straight ahead. He marches down the corner. The sound of furniture scraping the floor grows.
Jerry reaches the door, he peeks through the crack. He rams the door open with his shoulder.
In front of Jerry, Brick stands on a crooked bed (Star Wars sheets), he hangs by the window sill, one foot lifted to the window.
Brick turns to see the barrel of Jerry's gun. He falls down immediately onto the bed. He curls into fetal position.
Ahhh! Don't shoot! Don't please! I wanna live, I wanna-
Shut the fuck up Brick, I'm not gonna shoot you.
Brick tries to sit up. Jerry aims his gun again.
Brick rolls over. Jerry lowers his gun and steps to the edge of the bed.
What are you doing man? Is it really that bad?
Brick starts to whimper. A sniffle.
I'm-I'm sorry Jerry, I don't- I wanted to- she said I could hook up with her!
Yes, yes... I can't, sniff, I can't believe she, I didn't know okay. I just wanted a crew to hang and those guys, you know, and the drugs and the girls and the-
Y-Yes. I didn't know he was a criminal or anything, I swear dude. I didn't even- I was with Amanda most of the time anyways okay? I just talked with the guy and did drugs with him the one night.
Listen I have it in my phone, I'll give you the number okay!?
Jerry takes handcuffs out from his back pocket.
Don't worry I'm just taking you back to the station, after you give me the number I'll let you go.
Phew, Ay thanks man. Thanks for looking out for me.
It's good seein ya again dude.

scenes.heading: EXT. BRICK'S APARTMENT - LATER
content: Front door swings open to reveal Brick with both hand behind his back. Jerry follows close behind, keeping a loose grip on the handcuffs.
Could you uh, can you lock the door.
Should be in the ash tray by the door.
Jerry opens the door and leans inside. He reaches inside and leans back out with key in hand. He closes the door and locks it with his one free hand.
CAMERA follows them as they make their way past several apartment doors, then DRIFTS AHEAD, leaving the two men behind.
The window blinds are drawn but one hangs slightly tilted leaving a small gap, an eye can barely be seen peeking outside.
Jerry and Brick enter frame, crossing by the window. The ajar blind falls shut.
As the pass in front of the door, it bursts open to reveal a small elderly lady. This is MRS. WANTER.
Brandin? I knew all that commotion was you.
Jerry and Brick stop. Brick stands on the left, Jerry on the right, his hand loosely gripping Brick's cuffed wrists. Mrs. Wanter between them in the doorway.
What... What's going on here Brandin, who is this man?
Wait! Are you going to jail?! A little convenient to get arrested the day 'fore rent is due, isn't it Brandin?
He should be home later today.
Are you still going by Brick? You're 30 Brandin, why do you still want to act like a hooligan?
Oh well you boys have fun. You make sure to have him home soon.
She waves-mainly at Jerry-then shuts the door.
Brick shoots Jerry a smirk before they continue off screen.

scenes.heading: EXT. PARKING LOT - DAY
content: Jerry guides Brick toward an unmarked sedan.

Montage as Jerry opens the door for Brick, who takes a seat in the back and they drive through city(TBD). Strip malls, Franchise restaurants. Bland apartment complexes. A downtown that peaked in the 1980s.

scenes.heading: EXT. POLICE STATION - PARKING LOT - DAY
content: EXT. POLICE STATION - PARKING LOT - DAY
Jerry's unmarked sedan pulls into a spot. The lot is half full - a mix of police cruisers, personal trucks, and EVs.
THROUGH THE WINDSHIELD - Jerry. Eyes closed, taking deep breaths. Preparing himself.
Music swells, eyes open, he shakes it off.
Gets out, pops the trunk, grabs a black backpack.
Jerry walks through the parking lot, eyes mostly down.
Passes a neon green lifted truck - chrome everything. Windows tinted BLACK.
Jerry glances at it. Big exhale. Wipes his eyes.

scenes.heading: INT. POLICE STATION - CONTINUOUS
content: Inside now. Fluorescent lights. Linoleum floors.
A RECEPTIONIST (late-30s) sits at the front desk, focused on her computer.
He taps the desk twice. Continues towards the hallway.
Jerry walks through the flourescent light of the hallway. Past several doors with name placards he doesn't bother reading.
He enters the door marked: CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS DIVISION.

scenes.heading: INT. CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS DIVISION - CONTINUOUS
content: A cramped office. Five desks, three occupied. Heads down, typing, reading case files.
Jerry crosses to his desk near the back window, view of the parking lot. He drops his backpack on the floor.
He opens the drawer, pulls out a thick cream-colored folder, sets it on the desk.
CAMERA DRIFTS away from Jerry, to a door across the office labeled: LT. GREENISH - CRIMINAL INVEST.
The door opens. DETECTIVE STEVE WENTWORTH (40s, receding hairline), steps out. Coughs into his elbow, then totters toward the desks.
Stops before Jerry's desk. Jerry is reading a file while taking a sip from a Snoopy mug.
Greenish needs to talk to you.
Yeah, uh, let me just get my stuff settled I'll-
Wentworth plops down at his desk, the one directly across from Jerry. As he sits down, Jerry gets up and drops the file back in the drawer, shutting it harder than necessary.

scenes.heading: INT. LT. GREENISH'S OFFICE
content: The door cracks open and Jerry peeks inside with his head.

Greenish sits at a big desk, fancier than the shitty one Jerry uses. A clunky monitor sits on his desk, behind him are framed pictures of himself, and various presidents as well as certificates relating to police school.
Jerry takes a seat, Greenish pushes a brown folder across
Good, good. You know Jerry, you're one of our finest minds. Have I told you that before.
-Uh, well no sir but I mean- You might've told me, my memory sometimes you know-
Well, you are, this is why I'm putting you in charge of a very important case.
This is very important Jerry. And confidential. You are to work on this alone, okay?
I'm sorry I'm not sure I understand.
Jerry takes the folder and opens to the first document, CAMERA HOLDS ON Jerry as he reads.
This one comes from upstairs, it's of highest priority you keep this to yourself.
As Jerry scans further down the page, he grows confused as Greenish's words don't seem to match what he's reading.
Sir, it's says this is a missing persons case, possible homicide, I don't think one person-
Jerry places the folder on the desk and turns to the next document. Greenish points with two fingers to a name on the page: MAYA LUPREEDY.
Wait, she isn't married to Mayor-
Keep it down trooper! What did I say, no one else is to work with you on this, those are your orders.
Sorry sir, I just- I'm working with Wentworth on that stolen goods-
I know and you know damn well Wentworth isn't doing shit behind that door. It's you and that's final. Also watch your language Lefton, show some respect to the badge!
Sorry sir.... Just if I could ask why me? You usually put me on smaller stuff- hell, I mean, heck it's been at least a year since working that missing boy case downtown.
Greenish sighs, crosses his arms, and leans back into his chair.
You get on my nerves sometimes Lefton- but it's why I like you, ya keep me honest. You know President Lincoln kept his rivals in his cabinet?
He flips to the next page. Hold on - Jerry as he reads, he traces is finger along the paper to keep his place.
...I think I read about that in the-
Jerry reaches a word and stops, worry begins to flood his face.
Moving on, you've lived here most of your life Jerry. We think you might have certain connections-
These are people from my high school.
Well yeah, I thought that was implied with Maya.
Maya-Maya... Winston? Why is she married to the-

Jerry listen, I just talked with the sarge, and the mayor... And a few other people but not important for you to know. We think you're the one for this. I need you to understand how urgent the situation is.
It's you, you're our guy alright. Make us proud, we know you will.
Greenish stands, chest out, almost military, and motions towards the door. Jerry gets up, Greenish walks him to the door, opens it for him.
Jerry walks out of Greenish's office, the door shuts quickly behind him.
Jerry walks back to his desk, a latina woman, similar age, sits in his chair. This is DETECTIVE RAMIREZ.
Oh, hey Jerr. I need your help.
I can see that, now up.
Ramirez stands up. She leans against the side of the desk, practically sitting on it.
What're you talking to Greenish about?
That's exactly what I need help with!
Here just give me their name I'll have a report end of day.
Jerry sits down. He places the brown folder on the side of the desk not being sat on.
Wow. A case directly from Greenish. You suck his dick or something?
Something like that... It's nothing, just another stolen goods situation.
Nevermind, he still fuckin hates you.
Jerry stares at the brown folder. He leans back in his seat, eyes linger on the folder.
Ramirez hands a sticky note to Jerry. He sticks it on the monitor in front of him. She gets up off the desk.
Well? You gonna search. I gotta real case going.
Yeah someone stole shampoo, big whoop. Listen, this fuck-
Got caught with three girls, all minors, beat that!
Jesus christ dude. Probably shouldn't brag about that.
Ramirez gives Jerry a sly look, wags a finger at him playfully. Jerry's attention is still mostly on the brown folder. She walks back to her desk.
Jerry grabs the folder and gets up from his chair.

scenes.heading: EXT. POLICE STATION - PARKING LOT - DAY
content: EXT. POLICE STATION - PARKING LOT - DAY
Jerry sits in his sedan, reading the brown folder.
CAMERA DOLLIES into CU on Jerry through the windshield of his sedan.

scenes.heading: INT. JERRY'S SEDAN
content: ECU on the page Jerry is currently reading. We can see the name and picture of Brandin "Brick" Garrity.
CLOSE ON Jerry's face as his mouth falls agape.
You gotta be fuckin kidding me.

scenes.heading: INT. POLICE STATION - FRONT DESK - LATER
content: INT. POLICE STATION - FRONT DESK - LATER
Jerry is unlocking Brick's cuffs. Receptionist is still glued to the computer.
Jerry turns to the narrow hallway but there stands Lt. Greenish.
Jerry, who's this G.I. Joe lookin mother-
Just give him the number, he'll probably let you go.
Probably? You don't sound too sure.
Brick walks past Greenish into the hallway. Greenish
Solving the case and cleaning the streets at the same time. Doing good work Lefton, now back to it!
Greenish retreats into the hall. Jerry turns to the receptionist who's still locked on her screen.
What game is it today? Crossword or Pinball.
I thought Greenish just said get back to work.
Jerry exhales through his nose. He grins.

scenes.heading: EXT. SEDAN - EVENING
content: Jerry closes the brown case file in his lap, tosses it aside.
He closes his eyes. Takes a breath. Shakes it off.
He steps out of his sedan into--

scenes.heading: EXT. AMANDA'S APARTMENT
content: Badge in hand, he knocks on the door.
The shuffling of footsteps before the door cracks open.
Peeking through is a brown haired woman (30s) wearing a small tank top and OSCAR THE GROUCH pajama bottoms. This is MARY JOSEPH.
Hi Miss, I'm Detective Jerry Lefton I was just wondering if Amanda was home?
Oh.... Do you think she'll be back here tomorrow?
Is this about Maya? Are you investigating-
Jerry walks off. Mary leans in the door frame, dejected.

scenes.heading: EXT. AMANDA'S APARTMENT - NEXT MORNING
content: Jerry steps up to the door. He knocks.
Mary opens the door, same clothes. Messier hair.
Jesus christ, what time is it?
Like I said: I'm back to check if Amanda-
I know that, it's just- it hasn't even been, what? Ten hours?
Well I didn't have anything else on my checklist today so, this is the first thing I'm doing, like I said.
You know what I think you're doing detective?
You came back early, knowing Amanda wasn't going to be here. Cross another item off your checklist before closing this "missing person" case. Fuck off
I just- listen I'm sorry if it seems like I'm not doing my job, but trust me I'm doing my best to find Maya.
How about I come back later tonight, if she isn't here maybe you could answer a few questions for me?
Like hell I'm gonna tell you-
Or not! I just- I'm assuming you were a friend of Maya's? Am I correct?
Okay. Well then. If you have any information that could be of use, I'll be back tonight. Okay?
Jerry sighs, then walks away, head down. Mary leans on the door frame, smirk on her face.

scenes.heading: INT. SECURITY ROOM - BLACK BAZAAR
content: Ramirez leans in a door frame, same position as Mary. She has a less than pleased look.
She's listening to two men off screen arguing.
Just-just go back right there... yes! -no, no, no. Not there I said-
I don't... can you just give me some space man? It's not that easy as it-
Her view widens to reveal the subject of Ramirez's attention: Jerry hunched over a small computer and a young man (early 20s) fiddling with the controls.
They are watching security camera footage on a small monitor.
Yes! Right there! Ramirez, I need an opinion.
Ramirez pushes herself of the door frame. She stands to the side of the desk.
I'm sorry I thought you wanted-
Man, I didn't- maybe I should just get my boss.
Just let me- get out of the way.
That's not how it works, you need like a warrant I'm pretty sure.
Jerry motions for the young man to get up. The young man scowls back at Jerry. He stands.
Sorry about that. He can be a little ya know... just sometimes.
Whatever, I'm outta here, just don't break anything or my boss is gonna kick my ass.
He steps out, door still ajar. Jerry is already deeply focused on the screen. He's leaned forward, eyes almost touching the monitor.
See it's right here. I don't see why that kid couldn't just- I mean I barely know how computers work and I can still figure out a scroll wheel-
Jerry leans a bit back. Still forward in his chair.
Jerry hits the space bar, the video starts playing. Dmitri talks with Maya in an alleyway at night.
Yeah, looks like the photo you showed me.
The video ends with Dmitri passing a card to Maya. Maya walks off in one direction, out of view. Dmitri stays to talk on his phone.
Then he's like this for 3 minutes.
Jerry clicks slightly further on the video scroll bar. Dmitri get's off of his phone, then walks back through a door into the club.
I guess? Maybe he does it off camera, I don't have enough to be sure. You've barely told my anything about this case.
It's fine. This should be pretty clear cut. Now I just need to upload this...
Ramirez crosses her arms. Jerry leans forward. Focus back on the screen.
I don't know Jerry, from the point of this video, all I see is a man handing a girl a card then going about his business. Go further into the footage.
Ramirez I think you should stay out of this, I've got it figured now.
Ramirez takes hold of the mouse. She clicks forward.
Dmitri stands on his phone. Then goes back inside.
Now switch to the inside camera. See if he leaves.
Jerry looks at Ramirez with wide eyes. Trying to hide a grin.
Jerry clicks to another cam, further in the video: Dmitri is dancing sloppily with Brick, time stamp reads: 3:23:54 AM.
So this guy doesn't leave the entire night.
And we have- sorry, you have no clue where this girl goes after this video.
And you're saying he got her killed?
That's a big jump. Kidnapped, probably.
Holy... All I can do is guess Jerry. I know jack shit about this case, I can't- just-

What I don't get: To me, it looks like he gives her a card then makes a call then goes back inside the rest of the night. I know for a fact he wasn't the one to actually do it. Sure he might be implicated but we don't know that.
It's just, you see what I'm saying. He's all we got so far.
In the other room, the young man is talking with an older gentleman dressed in a polo at a bar. They both look over at the room.
Let's just go before you harass the employees any more.

scenes.heading: EXT. JERRY'S SEDAN - BLACK BAZAAR PARKING LOT - LATER
content: EXT. JERRY'S SEDAN - BLACK BAZAAR PARKING LOT - LATER
Jerry and Ramirez are sitting inside Jerry's sedan. Ramirez holds the brown case file in front of her.
I still can't figure out why Greenish put you on such an important case.
Must feel nice huh? Special treatment.
Jerry is struggling with his seatbelt, its caught.
Greenish promise something special if you solve it? A raise? A blow-
He just said he wanted me alone on it, is all. Confidentiality.
That's not it, you'd die before brown nosing that jarhead.
Jerry finally gets his seatbelt buckled. Ramirez sets the folder down.
That old piece of shit's gone senile on us.
Ramirez and Jerry stare at each other for a beat, serious. Before they can't hold back a small bit of laughter.
Thanks for coming by the way.
Explain to me why you needed me for some security tapes.

Uh well, the club owner's a prick to start. I mean it's why we only had pictures when he clearly has the tapes. Although it's obvious now they probably didn't have the bright minds to work a computer.
Okay? Still not sure why you dragged me along.
You're better with people. You think that old guy lets us in if I don't bring a young woman-
Fuck off. Just, you're better with people usually with these things so-so I guess I'm just saying-
Nah, it's fine. Don't mention it. Better than whatever the fuck I'm doing back at the station.
Ramirez looks out the window. Jerry drives off.

scenes.heading: EXT. JERRY'S SEDAN - STATION PARKING LOT - AFTERNOON
content: EXT. JERRY'S SEDAN - STATION PARKING LOT - AFTERNOON
Jerry's car pulls up to the curb of the station.
You sure you don't need anything from your desk?
I'm good, I packed everything for-
Ramirez steps out. Peeks back in.
Good luck. Hope you find your girl.
Ramirez chuckles. She pushes the door close.
Jerry accelerates before the door fully closes.
Ramirez stares at the car as Jerry drives off.

scenes.heading: EXT. JERRY'S APARTMENT - PARKING LOT - AFTERNOON
content: EXT. JERRY'S APARTMENT - PARKING LOT - AFTERNOON
Jerry pulls into a spot marked 303.
He gets out. Pops the trunk. Takes his backpack out.

scenes.heading: INT. JERRY'S APARTMENT - CONTINUOUS
content: The door unlocks. Jerry steps inside, wipes his feet on a clean welcome mat. No text. Gray.
Flicks on his lights. Three light switches. Then turns off one of them.
Jerry walks into the kitchen. He turns on a coffee maker.
He walks over to the couch, drops his bag.
He plops down. Wipes his face with his hands.
Something on the far wall catches his attention.
He gets up, crosses the room. A whiteboard--covered in notes about a stolen game console.
He grabs an eraser clears the board. Several plain black magnets sit in the corner.
Jerry walks back to the couch and opens his backpack.
He grabs the BROWN CASE FILE.
Walks back over to the whiteboard. Attaches the headshot of Maya in the center.
He grabs a blue marker draws a circle around her. Then a line to another circle. He attaches the security cam photo of Dmitri.
The light through the shades has slightly dimmed.
The whiteboard: now filled with photos and blue line connections, frantic notes. Maya's photo still at the center.
Jerry stands a foot away. Staring.
He looks down at his notebook, which he holds in front of his chest. A list of several locations.
He pockets the notebook. Turns around.
On a coffee table case files are scattered about. Jerry struggles to organize them.
He does, then slides them back into the brown case file. Then into his backpack. He zips it up.

scenes.heading: INT. SILVER DOLLAR DINER - AFTERNOON
content: An empty diner. A WAITRESS (aged 50s) wipes a counter.
Bells jingle as the door opens. Jerry enters. He wipes his feet down on a door mat.
-they were a rowdy group of kids, but never caused any kinda trouble.
The waitress holds a photo of Amanda. Jerry sits at the counter.
So you're sure you never saw her with anyone other than those kids?
Okay, well thanks for your time maam.
You sure I can't get anything for ya honey? Coffee's on the house for a city detective.
Jerry tries to hold back a smile.
Well good luck then, hope you find that girl.
Jerry takes the photo back. He swivels off his seat. Walks down the diner,

scenes.heading: INT. CATHY'S CAFÉ - AFTERNOON
content: Jerry is sitting back in a blue bean bag.
Across, a BARISTA (male, 20s), in a red bean bag. In between them a small circle coffee table.
I don't know dude. I see them sometimes, but I only work on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday. You know, so I don't see them that often.
Well how often would you say you've seen them.
Fair bit actually--now that I think about it.
Yeah was just them for the most part but, I don't know maybe they'd be hanging out with some boys. But no baldies, I'd deffo remember if they got a bald boy.
...You sure I can't talk to Cathy.
Both turn to look over their shoulders. A long line. Behind the counter, high school and college aged kids frantically manning machines, working the cash register.
A small lady wearing a neon purple apron, stitched on lettering: CATHY.
-You're going to burn the- just let me do it! Move!
The barista turns back to Jerry.
Yeah I see that. I'll leave you to it then, thanks for your help.
Jerry lumbers up from the bean bag. He walks out the door.
Through the window, past a sign for the café - Jerry walks out and around the corner.

scenes.heading: EXT. AMANDA'S APARTMENT - NIGHT
content: Jerry speed-walks around a corner to Amanda's building.
Slows at the entrance. He glances at some freshly planted flowers lining the walkway entrance. Marigolds.
Jerry goes to knock. The door opens.
This time, Mary is wearing a striped sweatshirt. And baggy jeans.
Jerry's worked up a small sweat.
Wanna come in? Or is this a take me to the holding cell kind of deal.
No, uh- is Amanda not here?
Of course not. So you wanna come in or no?

scenes.heading: INT. AMANDA'S APARTMENT - CONTINUOUS
content: Jerry steps inside. Mary makes her way to the kitchen.
Jerry goes to wipe his feet. There is no welcome mat.
Do you mind taking your shoes off? I like to keep dirt off our floors.
Jerry looks down. There is dirt all over the floor.
Jerry kicks his shoes off onto a pile of flip-flops and converse.
On the job, I get it. Water?
Mary pulls two glasses from a cupboard, a Brita from her fridge.
She walks into the living area. There are two couches arranged in an L shape, across from a small TV.
Jerry takes a seat on the far side of one couch. Mary sits on the close side of the other.
-Oh, guess we go right into it then. Uh-yeah this is pretty typical of her. Especially when she finds new people to party with.
No, well I met one of them. But just once when she decided to-
Jerry clicks a pen. Turns a page in his notebook.
White, tall--six footish, curly brown hair?
No I just said hi to the guy in passing really.
Okay... Does Amanda tell you where she's going?
Not usually, not this time. But she always shows up eventually. I've learned not to ask, saves me a lot of bitching.
Does Amanda have anywhere she likes to hangout? Restaurants, bars, secret bunkers?
Jerry looks down. He sits forward.
Did you try the Silver Dollar diner down on-
...Okay. We would meet a cafe nearby. I forget what it's called.
Cathy's Corner Coffee! Did you check there?
Jerry shows Mary his notebook: locations with all the names crossed out.
There is one place--I shouldn't though.
You shouldn't? The only things I know are in a thin brown case folder. Any secret spot, anything that only a friend would know.
Mary scrunches her face, then relaxes:
There is this one place where we would hang out a ton with our old friend group.
Yeah it's how we became roommates.. They still go there I'm pretty sure. Though I stopped hanging out with that crowd
It's a real hole in the wall, I'll say. Might not even be on a map. It's literally run out of an apartment. But the cook there, he's really chill, he runs the place. I've always liked him.
Well, that's great, do you have the address?
See, the thing is, this is kinda a sacred spot for some people. At least the people who I've seen go there. I'm not going to take away this safe space, because it got written in some police report.
Well you wouldn't understand, you're a cop.
What's that got to do... What happened to saving Maya?
Oh shit this really is the Maya case?
Yes! Did you not--what about the other night?
I was joking. I thought the mayor was trying to cover up her disappearance just before the election.
You should get off of social media.
So you just lick the boot then?
You're pretty rude, you know that.
Jerry leans back forward. Mary takes a sip of water, amused.
Just tell me, is this even a place worth investigating, why mention it at all?
Well, if Amanda isn't there, our group might be. At the least, one person there will know Amanda well. She goes there a ton. That's what she tells me when she's home.
For sure, someone will know her?
Okay, then write down the directions for me.
Can't do that copper. Take me with you.
I'm a great passenger princess, trust me I give great directions.
Mary stands up. Begins to tie her hair up.
No, that breaks probably a lot of rules or codes or-
You're not finding a way there without me. Plus they won't even let you inside without me.
No go copper. They don't like cops over there. Very liberal crowd.
Mary stretches her arms. Walks over to the door.
Yeah, it's Tuesday night they'll for sure be there.
Hey! What's with all the dirt?!
Jerry stands slowly, sees the dirt he tracked in.
I'll clean it when we get back.
Mary grabs his shoes and places them outside.

scenes.heading: EXT. AMANDA'S APARTMENT - CONTINUOUS
content: Jerry steps out in his socks. He jams his feet into his shoes. Loses balance on the second one. He slips, stumbles-
Hey watch the flowers, I just planted those.
Mary and Jerry walk around the corner out of sight.

scenes.heading: EXT. COOK'S APARTMENT COMPLEX - PARKING LOT - EVENING
content: EXT. COOK'S APARTMENT COMPLEX - PARKING LOT - EVENING
Jerry's sedan pulls in. Parks crooked, far walking distance from the curb.
402 you said? Alright, I won't take long.
He isn't going to talk to you
He won't care. He's not like you, he's chill.
Jerry opens his door, steps out. As he shuts his door: Mary's opens.
The fuck did I just--fuckit, like I care.
Mary gets out and skips past a grouchy Jerry.

scenes.heading: INT. COOK'S APARTMENT COMPLEX - HALLWAY
content: Just, stand back for a bit okay?
Mary and Jerry stand in front of a door labelled: 402.
She knocks 5 times in a pattern.
The door swings open to reveal THE COOK (late 60s).
He wears a dirty white apron and a bushy white Santa Claus beard.
My-my Mary. Our marigold has come home huh.
The cook leans forward into the door frame. Jerry comes into the cook's view.
Who is- Mary who is this? Couldn't be little Ethan right?
Jerry spins around. The cook scans him up and down.
He's... Just my ride. He's not important-
Jerry is displeased at this comment.
You wanna wait here for a little bit?
He can wait in the car.
What the fuck- you're not even supposed to be here! How about you wait?
Now you dont talk to her-
Jerry holds his badge out in front of him. Flashes it.
I'm Detective Jerry Lefton with the city-
Hold on now, Mary who is this? Why did you bring this man here?
No it's okay I promise just let me-
Just shut the fuck up okay? Please?
How could you bring this cop here Mary? I haven't even seen you in months!
Behind the three of them, a door marked 401 swings open.
In the door way stands an old lady.
Will you people be quiet? It's my bedtime Norman you know that!
Sorry Renee, these two were just-
Don't make me call the landlord!
The old lady huffs and slams the door shut.
The cook lets out a heavy sigh.
It was nice seeing you again Mary, but maybe not on these terms.
Now if you two would leave.
Fucking waste of my- let's go.
Please, it's about Maya. And Amanda.
Amanda's name catches the cook's attention.
The cook looks Jerry up and down one more time.
Alright, come in. But! No talking with anyone inside. Talking to the pig.

scenes.heading: INT. COOK'S APARTMENT - CONTINUOUS
content: The cook leads them into the apartment.
A small abode, set up with a few folding tables, with folding chairs.
A haze in the air. Maybe food. Maybe pot.
At one of the tables, a group of 4 young adults (college age). Dressed in different black alt and gothic clothes. Dyed hair and piercings.
They all peek a look over at the new visitors.
The cook stops at a corner table, far from the others.
Amanda was here last week, you know. We had a nice conversation about women's volleyball. But, uh, that group there Mary, she's still with 'em.
Jerry grabs his notebook in his pocket. It gets stuck, trying to get it out.
Jerry tries to hide the fact he is struggling with his jacket:
Yeah great times, love those guys.
No! Of course not. Let's stop with the inside jokes. I have no fucking clue what you people are talking about.
Need something? I got tea, coffee-
Jerry finally gets his notebook out. Clicks his pen.
...okay then. A bit after Mary here left, your little group, started getting, not-so-little. I vetted them of course but, I don't know. Amanda just seemed out of it the last few times we've talked.
Well, of course they started coming over less, although I don't mind that. But the stuff I hear them talking about. Their adventures have gotten a little adventurous let's just say-

When I first met them, when I first met Mary, they loved the calm and peace of this place. The restaurants and bars they talked about going to were all quaint, hole in the wall type of place. But now- I don't know, I shouldn't judge.
Jerry tosses his notebook on the table. And the pen.
Okay let's try this: you finish your thought, we get out.
Oh, why should I tell you anything. They're good kids!
They could be the Beatles for all I care. You protecting them right now, is directly getting in the way of me finding Maya.
Cook leans back. Somber look as he stars at Jerry.
And you're with the city police-
...They would talk about their outings at these fancy clubs recently. They've been hanging out with people from these places, even asked if they could come here.
Hell no, these aren't good people.
What do mean? How would you know?
Like I said: I vet everyone who wants shelter here.
What was so bad about these people?
Rich. Corrupt. Old money trust fund kids.
Having a lot of money doesn't make you a bad person.
I'd argue not, but I ain't arguing with a pig.
The cook smiles at Jerry. Mary smiles at the cook.
These are people with ties to government figures. They can't get in trouble. These spoiled brats have never experienced consequence. It's a foreign concept to them.
In fact, last time that group was here, they were talking about all the coke they were able to snort for free at a mansion party. They talked about this crazy European man.
Ah no, just mentioned he had a funny accent. Said he was the hardest partier they've seen.
They mention anything about him being bald?
Now that you say... I think they did.
Jerry perks up in his seat. He scribbles something down in his notebook.
You said something about government ties, are you talking about the Mayor.
Lupreedy? That bastard. Wouldn't be surprised if he did Maya in himself...
Jerry looks down at his lap, at his notebook. He scans down the page with his eyes.
Thank you Norman. All of this is has been extremely helpful.
Oh it's okay, it was very nice to see you Mary. Please come back sometime, okay?
Thank you so much. I'm so sorry about-
Jerry stands by the door. He's wiping his feet on the welcome mat.
Mary smiles at the cook before taking off with Jerry.

scenes.heading: EXT. COOK'S APARTMENT COMPLEX - PARKING LOT - NIGHT
content: EXT. COOK'S APARTMENT COMPLEX - PARKING LOT - NIGHT
Jerry is marching confidently across the lot to his sedan.
Mary lags behind walking, arms crossed.
You're a real dick, you know that?
Why'd you have to be such an asshole to him? He's just a sweet old-
Why's that old creep got kids at his place?
Hey! You can't call him a creep. You don't know him.
That's not weird? It's not creepy like at all?
Jerry and Mary are now yelling at each other across the parking lot.
Nice? He called me a pig.
Like you said: he doesn't know me. You don't know me. Where does he get off calling me- I'm trying to save a missing person here!
You call this trying? One man going door to door, like a knife salesman? What the fuck kinda operation-
Mary turns, Jerry leans to see past her. One of the girls from the apartment.
You guys were asking about Maya right? You're trying to find her?
Yes. Well he is. He's a detective.
I might know where she was last seen.
Jerry sits up front with alt girl. Mary sits in the back middle seat.
Jerry has his pen and notebook out.
-last time she texted me, it lines up with her disappearing.
Just to double check, this is the address right?
Jerry shows her the notebook. In big lettering:
My god, it's just- what could've happened there?
I was talking about it with some of Amanda's friends. They think drugs, or she eloped, it could be a lot of things.
She doesn't- it doesn't sound liker her to go party with some douche.
And no mention of any bald people there?
...Uh, I don't think we really talked about the hairstyles of other people. I guess.
Ah, well thanks this is a ton of help.
Please find her. She was a very kind soul.
The alt girl gets out the car, closes the door.
Mary clumsily climbs into the passenger seat. Accidentally, hits Jerry in the side of his head with her shoe.
She readjusts and buckles her seatbelt.
Weird fucking group going on here.
Jerry's starting to break a little.
No, honestly, I want to know. Of all places, some dudes dank-ass apartment. I mean, I don't like clubs or bars either but damn. Would rather stay home than hang with some bum.

You wouldn't- Listen there are some people in the world who have known nothing but rejection and exclusion and prejudice for reasons completely out of their control. See I can believe you being lonely because you're a miserable fuck, but some people are lonely because the world is cruel.
Yeah I bet that old white man suffered a LOT of prejudice.
Jerry chuckles to himself starting the car. Mary snaps:

That man was drafter to 'Nam, he was gay living in the south. He doesn't have friends from there. He doesn't have family. You don't understand, you will never understand. So just shut up and do your fucking job!
Silence. The low rumble of the car. I wasn't-
Jerry stares at his shoes for a second.

I'm sorry I'm getting so worked up it's just- All I want is to find this girl, it's the first real case I've ever had in 2 years of service. I just want to find her, and when people get in the way of that by--being people--it's crushing. Like I can hear the minutes- the seconds of her life ticking away in the back of my head.
Mary looks more softly at Jerry now.
I know I didn't know this girl okay, especially like you did. But the burden of her life, of bringing someone back from the dead is on me. And I'll be damned before I let that happen.
It... wasn't right for your boss to put this entire case on you.
I know. Doesn't change the fact it still is all on me... Sorry about my behavior. Would you, uh, tell him I'm sorry next time you see him?
Jerry releases the hand brake. His sedan pulls out of the lot.
Mary is softly smiling, looking out the window.

scenes.heading: EXT. MARY'S APARTMENT - PARKING LOT - NIGHT
content: EXT. MARY'S APARTMENT - PARKING LOT - NIGHT
Jerry's sedan pulls up to the curb.
He gets out, goes to open Mary's door. She opens it before he can.
Mary steps out. Starts to walk off.
I said I'm sorry, I was being mean earlier.
He cracks a smirk. The happiest Jerry's been so far.
And thank you--for looking for her--I didn't think anyone was.
Mary turns back around walks off.
Cachet du Vois - "If Only" (melancholic Rnb) plays throughout.
A) EXT. MARY'S APARTMENT - Jerry leans on the hood of his car. Watches Mary until she turns a corner out of his sight. He pushes himself up, walks around to the driver side.
B) EXT. CITY STREETS - Jerry's sedan cruises through town.
C) EXT. PARK - The sedan passes. Some teenagers loitering.
D) EXT. POLICE STATION - The sedan passes. Only light still on is LT. GREENISH's office.
E) EXT. JERRY'S APARTMENT COMPLEX - The sedan pulls into parking spot 303

scenes.heading: INT. JERRY'S APARTMENT - NIGHT
content: Flicks light switches on. Turns one of them back off.
Drops his backpack by the door. Locks it.
Walks into the kitchen, Jerry's full apartment comes into view for the first time.
Minimalist. Only the essentials. A couch. A table.
Kitchen counter has a toaster and a cheap Keurig.
Only thing hanging is the whiteboard in the living room.
Jerry walks out of the kitchen Garfield mug in hand.
Sits down, takes a sip. Grimaces.
Sets the mug down. The table stained with water rings.
Stares across the room. At the whiteboard.
At the center of his attention: MAYA. Her picture sits in a the middle of a web of scribbles and news clips.
He jumps out of his seat. Grabs his keys and backpack.
Coffee still on the table steaming.

scenes.heading: INT. SILVER DOLLAR DINER - LATER
content: Jerry stares into a half-full mug of cold coffee. His notepad beside it, covered in cramped scribbles.
Jerry looks up. The YOUNG WAITRESS (young 20s, energetic) leans over the counter.
Oh yeah. There's this gay dude- or maybe non-binary? I think he wore a dress, I mean she-
Let's stick to what you saw.
-more recently, they've been bringing these total creeps... It's horrible for business you know? Scares the customers-
Total losers. Greasy hair, tight pants-
She holds her fingers a centimeter apart. Jerry stares at the space.
Like, dealers or something. Always bragging about money and connections.
Best places to score, party. Like I give a fuck where these guys swing their-
A club. A bizarre black something.
Jerry flips to a page in his notepad.
The Black Bazaar, ugh! Total sleaze fest.
Yeah, been once. Smelled like dick-
Jerry slides a ten across the counter, already standing.
That's it? I got way more dirt on that skank-
Amanda stiffed me on a check once! It was over fifty dollars!
But Jerry's gone. She pockets the cash, dumps the old coffee.

scenes.heading: EXT. SILVER DOLLAR DINER - NIGHT
content: Jerry exits out the glass doors.
Looks both ways. Takes off right.

scenes.heading: EXT. BLACK BAZAAR - NIGHT
content: Jerry's sedan cruises down an industrial strip. Warehouses, abandoned stores. A purple glow washes over the car.

scenes.heading: INT. JERRY'S SEDAN - CONTINUOUS
content: Jerry stares at his notepad, held inches from his face. Circled four times: BLACK BAZAAR.
He's stopped, squinting at a building. In front of him: a PACKED parking lot. Luxury cars, limos.
A purple vested valet takes keys from an elderly man hobbling out of a purple Mercedes.

scenes.heading: EXT. BLACK BAZAAR - PARKING LOT - CONTINUOUS
content: EXT. BLACK BAZAAR - PARKING LOT - CONTINUOUS
Jerry pulls into a spot, in between a yellow Lambo and a blacked out Range Rover.
Gets out. Nervously adjusts his tie.
The building: a black cube. No windows.
A neon purple sign floods the lot with light.
A LINE of PEOPLE snakes from the entrance.
By the door, a massive BOUNCER (late 30s, Polynesian) checks a clipboard. He holds onto a purple velvet rope.
I'm actually a detective. I'm with the city. Need to speak with your boss.
Bouncer looks up. Scans Jerry, takes in  his nervous energy.
Jerry pats his pockets - jacket, pants, jacket again. Fumbles for it in his jacket. Shows it to the bouncer
Aw sweet. Yeah, go ahead man.
The bouncer holds the door open for Jerry. Purple light flashing out. Bass pulsing. Jerry steps into--

scenes.heading: INT. BLACK BAZAAR - CONTINUOUS
content: Jerry steps inside. Electronic club music pulsing, louder than expected.
The club is packed. Hordes of people crowd around tables and couches. The dance floor a blur of bodies. Everything's washed in purple light.
Jerry tries to squeeze through the crowd.
He pinballs off dancers and drunk club-goers. Someone spills a drink on his jacket. He doesn't notice.
Jerry watches the dance floor. Bodies throwing themselves around to the beat.
In the crowd - a flash of Maya's hair. He turns. Not her.
Even Mary's silhoette by the bar. A stranger.
Jerry stands still. The crowd flows around him.
His trance is broken by a guy running backwards into him.
The club drunk wobbles back to his table. A group of people cheer him on as he falls over the table. Face first into a pile of coke.
Jerry continues pushing through until he emerges into a less crowded part near the back.
He leans over. Catches his breath. Adjusts his tie.
At the VIP section, the CLUB OWNER (60s, gray beard) holds court with several young women.
Jerry marches over. Stops at the velvet rope.
Hello young man, looking for a nice time, eh? You look like you need a good time. Let the boy in-
The club owner looks up at Jerry. Scratches his beard.
I don't know if you remember from earlier-
Wait a second. Aren't you the cop who harrassed by employee?
That was my nephew you bastard! In the security room!
When he turns back to Jerry - gone. Swallowed by the crowd.

scenes.heading: EXT. BLACK BAZAAR - ALLEYWAY - NIGHT
content: Jerry bursts out the side door.
He leans on the wall. Catches his breath.
His head falls back. Directly above him - a security camera.
Pointed down the alleyway at the exact angle from the Dmitri-Maya photo.
He heads back down the alley toward the street.
At the front door, there's a second bouncer now talking with the first one.
Jerry approaches. The new bouncer is even bigger.
Hey, yeah. I was wondering if you had security cameras on the front of the building.
He points up to a camera right above the door.
Nothing that captures the parking lot? The curb?
Jerry glances at a gnarly shark skull tattoo on his neck. Clears his throat.
Mind if I ask you a few questions?
Aw yeah, I'm just about to take my break.
The bouncer starts walking. Jerry has to quickstep to keep up.
How often do you work here?
Most nights, for about a year.
They stop at the alley entrance. The bouncer leans against the brick wall, making Jerry look even smaller.
Know a guy named Dmitri? He's bald.
Aw yeah, I love that guy. Sweet dude.
Sweet dude? He's... You sure we're talking about the same guy?
Russian Dmitri? Yeah man, he's the best. Total party animal but he never causes trouble.
Uh... Yeah. Does he ever... Take anyone home? Girls specifically?
Dmitri? Naw man. He's here till we close. Every time.
Jerry taps his pen against the notepad.
So you've never seen him leave with anyone? In a cab or car?
Naw. I even buy him an Uber sometimes. Heh.
Drinks too much. Gets too high. Lotta reasons. But he's always good for it with the money.
Jerry's pen hovers over his notepad. Jerry sways, dazed in confusion.
Are there any girls he hangs out with regularly? The names Amanda or Maya ring any bells?
Naw he doesn't hang out with girls man. He's homosexual.
Then why would he be hanging out with Maya in this alleyway?
Bouncer thinks about this. Really thinking.
Maybe she needed something? Dmitri knows everyone. All the parties and stuff.
Like, he always knows where things are happening. Who's throwing what and when.
I guess? I just know people ask him stuff sometimes. Where to go, who to talk to.
You wouldn't happen to have his home address?
Aw... Sorry man, I can't do that, I don't want to rat on my boy.
Yeah... No, I understand. Thanks for your time.
Totally man. Hope you find what you're looking for.
The bouncer heads back to the door. Jerry watches him go, then looks down at his notepad.
He's circled "GAY" next to a four times circled "DMITRI".

scenes.heading: EXT. BLACK BAZAAR - PARKING LOT - NIGHT
content: EXT. BLACK BAZAAR - PARKING LOT - NIGHT
Jerry is dead asleep inside his car. Mouth agape, saliva dripping off his chin.
A drunk homeless man hobbles up to the passenger side door.
He leans over the curb, falling on the hood. A loud thud.
Jerry's head slowly rocks back and forth. Eyes barely start to peel.
A STREAM OF PISS hits the passenger side window. The drunk man has propped himself against the car.
Jerry stretches in his seat. Wipes his chin and rubs his eyes.
He lays back down to catch one last second of sleep.
His head rocks to the right. His eyes widen.
The drunk man is whistling away, still pissing.
Jerry grabs some files from the passenger seat and tosses them at the window.
Get the fuck out of here!
He looks at Jerry, giggles to himself. Hikes his pants up.
Jerry sits up in his car, watching in awe.
He bunches up the papers, scattered around the car. Slides them back into their folder.
Props the seat back up, and buckles himself in. He inserts the keys and starts the car.
The digital clock on the dash flashes on: 9:27 AM.
Jerry leans forward in his seat exhausted.
He starts banging his head against the wheel.

scenes.heading: INT. POLICE STATION - RECEPTION - MORNING
content: An analog clock on the wall reads 9:44, ticks over to 45.
The receptionist is hunched over her desk. Almost breathing on the monitor in front of her.
She looks up, through the glass doors.
Jerry is hustling up the stairs.
He bursts in the room out of breath. Hands on knees.
Wipes his feet on the entrance mat then marches forward.
Past the receptionist desk. The receptionist's eyes still tracking Jerry.
Jerry comes to a halt. Adjusts his tie.
Jerry stares down the hallway. Takes a deep breath.
He continues off, pace a bit slower this time.
The receptionist is already back in her monitor. Hasn't noticed Jerry's left.
You gotta four letter word for-

scenes.heading: INT. POLICE STATION - CRIMINAL INVEST. - CONTINUOUS
content: INT. POLICE STATION - CRIMINAL INVEST. - CONTINUOUS
Jerry pushes the door open with his shoulder. He stops just as he enters, staring into the office.
Staring back: Detectives Ramirez and Wentworth. Sitting at their desks, concerned looks.
Jerry continues through the office into-
Jerry carefully handles the door knob, enough so he can slide inside.
Listen I'm really sorry lieutenant, I got sidetracked following up on-
After closing the door behind him, Jerry sees Greenish is not seated at his desk.
He looks around the office: window blinds are drawn, cracked enough so that rays of light cut through the office.
Silhouetted by these rays, a man. A stout, big-bodied man. His husky voice rumbles out in the office:
Jerry's expression is beyond confusion. He carefully takes a seat, gaze locked on the man.
The man heaves a cough into his elbow. Wipes his forehead with a handkerchief. He turns around to Jerry.
The man (60s) has a balding gray head of hair. Wears a navy blue suit, red tie, and a white shirt that is stressing at the buttons.
You know who I am son?
Jerry leans closer to get a better view of his face. A pin on the man's lapel catches a ray of light and flashes Jerry. An American flag pin.
Don't watch the news, huh? No social media?
The man walks behind Greenish's desk. Stops under a photo that catches Jerry's eye: Greenish shaking hands with the man.
And would you have a modicum of an idea as to why your Mayor has taken time out of his busy schedule to meet with you-
He reads a line off a paper in front of him.
Well I mean if I had to, uh, guess sir--it would probably be... it would probably be that, um, case. Should I--am I okay, I mean--are we okay to talk about the case, uh-
Yeah that one, so I guess it's cool if we talk about it-
My wife's case Jerry! Are you anywhere close to closing my wife's case at all?!

Well, I'm getting somewhere, I'd say. It's just tough- Greenish said that I'm the only one who should be working on this, and that, uh, I shouldn't talk about this with anyone? Not to be a snitch on my own boss but it seems like he hasn't put a lot of care-

Jerry I'll give you your props where they are due. Hassling that boy for the man's address was a great start. So you know where the man lives, what work is there to do detective? It's a pretty shut and close case I'd say. What in Saint Mary's name could you have possibly been doing these past couple days, besides dawdling?
I told Greenish to make this easy on you. This should be a layup for your career Jerry! I'm trying to help you out son.
I'm not sure I- sir, a lot of the work I've done so far, this whole thing is way more complicated than the case file.
Complicated? The only thing complicating this case is you detective.
Do I have to do your damn job for you? Let me make this very easy for you detective: find this Dmitri fella that was fraternizing with my wife, and arrest that motherfucker.
Well mister... Mayor, I have good reason to believe Dmitri had nothing to do with the disappearance of your wife.
The mayor leans back in his seat, stares out the window.
I mean, sure I don't know where she could be but, uh, at least we know she might not be kidnapped. Silver lining way of things I guess being that there's a higher chance your wife will be found-
Mayor Lupreedy slams his fist on the desk. Rises over Jerry in a rage.
Can't you just arrest that damn commie bastard that took my wife!
Jerry sits back, stares at his lap.
The mayor catches his breath. Fixes a button that came undone on his shirt.
Sorry to yell at you son. But this is how the job is, okay? Now let's close this case and just be done with all this nastiness.
He starts for the door. Jerry interrupts him:
Mayor lays a hand on his shoulder.
A single tear falls down his cheek.
You're a good guy Jerry. That's rare in this world so, let's keep it that way.
The mayor leaves out the room. Jerry is stunned.
He takes a moment to collect himself.
Greenish bursts into the room. Coffee in hand.
How'd yer meeting with the Mayor go Lefton?
Can you turn the light on, on your way out Detective, creepin' me out there, sitting in the dark like that.
Jerry snaps out of it. Get's up to leave.
S-Sorry about that sir. I'll go.

scenes.heading: INT. POLICE STATION - CRIMINAL INVEST. - CONTINUOUS
content: INT. POLICE STATION - CRIMINAL INVEST. - CONTINUOUS
Jerry steps back into the office. Both detectives are now gone.
He walks over to his desk. A post-it placed at the center.
It reads an address. Under it the name: DMITRI ONGLESTOV.

INT. SILVER DOLLAR DINER - NIGHT

A plain white mug sits on the counter. Half full, cold.

The sound of light restaurant chatter.

Jerry sits at a counter stool. Talking with a younger waitress (young 20s).

YOUNG WAITRESS
-oh yeah, Amanda's a real bitch. That whole group is full of weirdos. You can just tell-

(reading notepad)
You said more recently-

-more recently, they've been bringing these total creeps... It's horrible for business you know? Scares the customers-

Could you be more descriptive, like, appearance-wise.

Loser-types, like, they look like they came out of Jersey Shore. You know Jersey Shore?

Tight pants. Greased back hair. The whole deal. Pretty sure these dudes live at the club. I mean I'm sure cus they it's all they talk about.

They talked to you about the club?

No... I just overhear em. They come in so late anyways, they're literally the only ones in here most of the time, how can I not-not listen to them.

So the guys like talking about the club?

YOUNG WAITRESS
Well yeah, that and drugs. Pretty sure these dudes are like, their dealerrs. Make sure you write that down. The drugs part. They were talking about doing coke and-

Look I'm not here for- Any clubs specifically?

YOUNG WAITRESS
The Black Bazaar. I've actually been there, only once though. My boyfriend suggested it, well his friend suggested it-

-I don't know, the place seems kinda douchey you know? Makes sense cus his friends a total douchebag. Such a bad influence on my sweetie bear, talked him into buying not one but two lap dances! Total sleaze-

JERRY

Oh really? Take then care mister-detective.

The young waitress smiles as Jerry swivels up out of his seat. She grabs his mug and wipes the counter down.

Jerry walks through the half-busy diner as he pockets his notepad.

EXT. BLACK BAZAAR - NIGHT

Jerry's sedan pulls up to the curb of the parking lot. In the background, a completely full lot.

Jerry opens the door, gets out. Steps to the sidewalk.

He looks up at the now lit pylon sign. 

In neon purple lettering: The BLACK BAZAAR.

Jerry walks through the parking lot. Taking glances at limos and Range Rovers. Expensive sports cars in a variety of bright colors.

The club: a plain, black building without windows.

A long line extends out from the door. By it stands a large, muscular New Zealander man.

JERRY
Uh... Excuse me sir.

BOUNCER
Ah 'sup man.

Ay not you brother.

Sorry 'bout that man.

JERRY

BOUNCER
You gotta badge.

BOUNCER
Awe sweet man. Yeah you can come in.

What the fuck dude?

CLUB MALE 2
That's totally not fair man!

Jerry steps inside. Electronic club music pulsing.

JERRY
(to Bouncer)
Thanks.

He pinballs off of dancers and drunk club-goers.

CLUB DRUNK
Watch it dickbag!

JERRY
S-Sorry.

The club drunk wobbles back to his table. A group of people cheer him on as he falls over the table. Face first into a pile of coke.

He leans over to catch his breath.

Jerry marches over to the bar.

JERRY
Excuse me sir-

CLUB OWNER
Hello young man, looking for a good time. You look like you're looking for a good time. 

He gestures at the women who sit with him.

JERRY
No sir, actually-

CLUB OWNER
Take your pick! I know what you want: a blonde girl, right? You look like a blonde lover, eh?
(chuckles)
You look like, uh...

He scratches his gray beard.

CLUB OWNER
Wait a second. Aren't you the cop who harrased my workers? That was my nephew you know!

JERRY
Ah... Listen, I'm sorry-

CLUB OWNER
No, get out. Out now!
(to bartender)
Call security. Get security!

When he turns back to Jerry, he's gone.

Jerry bursts out the side door. Into the dimly lit alleyway.

He leans on the wall. Catches his breath.

His head falls back. Directly above him, he spots: a security camera.

It's pointed down the alleyway. Same angle as the Dmitri and Maya photo.

He walks down the alley back to the curb.

A cab pulls up.

CLUB GIRL (O.S.)
Over here!

A girl runs past Jerry. Arms waving in the air.

Jerry looks at her run by, then looks back the other way.

He jumps backwards out of the way before a group of several more girls storm by.

He watches as they pack into the cab like it's a clown car.

He looks back to the front door.

There's a second bouncer now talking with the first one.

Jerry walks back up to him.

JERRY
Uh, hey it's me.

BOUNCER
Aw 'sup man.

JERRY
Hey, yeah. I was wondering of you had security cameras on the front of the building.

BOUNCER
Just the one.

Nothing that captures the parking lot? Even the curb here?

Aw yeah, I'm just about to take my break here.

BOUNCER 2
See ya.

Most nights, for about a year.

BOUNCER
Aw yeah, totally.

JERRY

BOUNCER
Aw yeah, I love Dmitri. Sweet dude.

BOUNCER

So you've never seen him leave in a cab with anyone, or take anyone home in a car?

Naw. I even buy him an Uber sometimes. Heh.

Naw he doesn't hang out with girls man. He's gay.

Dmitri's gay?

Jerry whips out his notepad. Clicks his pen.

So if a girl came to him, it was information for a party--For drugs.

Yeah probably.

JERRY
And you knew Dmitri?

BOUNCER
Aw yeah we're best buds.

JERRY
Do you have his address.

BOUNCER
Aw... Sorry man, I told you a lot already, I don't want to rat on my boy.

JERRY
Yeah... No it's fine. You gave me a lot to think about anyway. Have a good night sir.

BOUNCER
Totally man. Take care. Hope you figure out what you're looking for.

...Thanks.

A drunk man hobbles to the passenger side of the car, on the sidewalk.

The sound of liquid pattering on pavement.

What the fuck!

Ah shit-

Props the seat back up, starts the car.

Jerry is hustling up the stairs.

No... You got a five letter word for: It's buried then comes to life.

Yeah.

Jerry walks in. Immediately, Ramirez and Wentworth stare over at him.

Serious stares. 

Jerry points at Lt. Greenish's door. Ramirez shrugs back at him.

.LT. GREENISH'S OFFICE - CONTINUOUS

Jerry walks inside, closes the door behind him.

JERRY
Sorry I'm late sir, I was doing-

VOICE (O.S.)
Detective Lefton? Is that correct.

A big, fat man stands by the window, looking into the parking lot. Green truck in the distance.

JERRY
Uh, yeah, Jerry. Jerry Lefton... Is Leiutenant-

VOICE
Do you know who I am Jerry?

The man turns to face Jerry. He's silhoetted by the sunlight.

JERRY

MAYOR LUPREEDY
You do watch the news then?

JERRY
I'm sorry, is Greenish... Is this about the Maya case?

MAYOR LUPREEDY
Yes the missing persons case. I've heard you've been hard at work.

The mayor plops in his seat. It creaks under his weight.

JERRY
Well, it is your wife sir. I'm trying my hardest to.

MAYOR LUPREEDY
Well obviously not hard enough. What, it's been almost half a week and this case still isn't closed.

JERRY
I'm going as fast as I can, I swear. I'm the only one working on it right now, it's hard-

The mayor slams his fist on the table.

MAYOR LUPREEDY
Is it so hard to arrest that Commie bastard that took my wife?!

JERRY
Sir, I... I'm not sure if Dmitri was the one who took Maya. I've been asking around.

MAYOR LUPREEDY
Oh I know Jerry. Don't get me started--you are harrasing the fine people of this town, my town. Over what? 

Jerry leans forward. Gets serious:

JERRY

MAYOR LUPREEDY
Last night you harassed poor Mister Al-Mahmoud down at the double B.

JERRY
Double b?

MAYOR LUPREEDY
The black bazaar? You need to get out more son-

JERRY
Sir I have real reason to believe Dmitri had nothing to do with the disappearance of Maya-

The mayor erupts. He rises, laudes over Jerry.

MAYOR LUPREEDY
I don't care! Listen here you two bit Sherlock Holmes wannabe! You close this case today or you are in deep.

He leans close.

MAYOR LUPREEDY
You don't want part of this son.

Jerry looks down at his lap. Takes a breath.

MAYOR LUPREEDY
Now, that ruffian boy you brought in the other day, gave us the Ruskis address. The job is-

Jerry looks up at the Mayor. Face scrunched.

JERRY
She's your wife... She might still be alive. How can you not...

MAYOR LUPREEDY
I'd stop my chatter right about now, if I we're you.

Jerry falls back in his seat. The mayor walks to the door.

He grabs the handle.

MAYOR LUPREEDY
You seem like a good guy Jerry. Let's keep it that way, stay out of this.

The mayor leaves. Door hangs open.

Jerry is stun-locked in his chair. Mouth agape.

Greenish marches in, coffee in hand.

GREENISH
You're lucky you know! Not many people are personally requested by the Mayor himself! It's an honor.

JERRY
...Yeah.

Greenish sits in his chair. Stares at Jerry looking at the ground.

GREENISH
You okay son? Snap out of it! You got work to do.

JERRY
Yeah. Sorry.

GREENISH
Don't embarass me Jerry. Mayor's watching me just as much as you.

Jerry carries himself up out of his seat. He exits the room.

Dmitri Onglestov?

DMITRI
(not looking)
This is me. Who is asking?

JERRY
I'm detective Jerry Lefton with the city criminal investigations-

Jerry flashes his badge.

You are cop.

Yeah, sure. Listen Dmitri it doesn't matter what my job title is exactly, just know, you are in a lot of trouble here.

Me? I am in no trouble. I do nothing wrong.

Maya.

My what? My a what?

Jesus christ, you don't even remember her name? Maya Lupreedy!

Yes.

And?

This is you.

Yeah.

You're not denying it.

Why would I? Was fun night.

Never done coke off someone's behind?

Ah. Okay, I understand now. Come brother sit down.

Dmitri do you understand that this girl is missing. Last seen the night of this photo.

Hmm. I see. No this is not last of Lupreedy girl.

Explain.

See I give her card. In photo.

I mention I know rich guy, he throw party. The girl wanted to go party. Who am I to deny her, you know?

Wait so, Maya did go to a party later that night?

DMITRI
I think so.

You think?

DMITRI
I just buy Uber ride for her. I never went to this party. I stay with that American boy doing-

I think I get the picture.

Would you mind writing down the address for me?

DMITRI
Listen Jerry, you come to my house and accuse me of these things I'm not sure how I feel to help right now.

JERRY
Dmitri listen-

DMITRI
I just fuck with you, American cop
(laughs)
Don't worry Jerry, I help, you seem like good guy.

JERRY
Oh well, uh thanks. And yeah sorry about that, it's just procedure you know? We didn't even know about this party until-

DMITRI
You not find out about party already. Wow, you are bad cops.

JERRY
Why? Was this a well known event?

DMITRI
No, no. This was powerful man, very powerful man.

JERRY
The mayor.

DMITRI
Jerry, please. Let me finish. 

JERRY
Sorry.

DMITRI
Is okay. You know salt? This guy he finds the salt in the ground and sells it to the burger comapanies, the fast food guys. You like Little Ceasars?

Dmitri opens a box of half eaten pizza that sits on a coffee table in front of him.

JERRY
I'm impartial.

DMITRI
Is very good, yes?

JERRY
Wait so this guy owns salt mines, is what you're saying?

DMITRI
Yes.

JERRY
Why is a salt mine tycoon throwing parties for little-

DMITRI
No no no. Hahaha. Not this man. Is his son.

JERRY
His son.

DMITRI
Yes, the rich fuck already gifted the boy a mansion for his 20th birthday. Is big conspiracy, you think?

JERRY
Well... I've found some things - you know - I guess, I guess I just don't understand why the state would want to cover this up so badly.

DMITRI
State is cover up?

JERRY
Trying to.

DMITRI
Lupreedy, guy not girl, said he would cut back on health money for food. I have seen on the news. Salt man is most likely in Lupreedy guy's pocket. Lupreedy and state need to cover up death to keep power and salt guy need to save his boy.

JERRY
....Holy shit.

DMITRI
Is big conspiracy, no?

JERRY
Uh, yes I guess so... Um listen Dmitri thanks for your help. I'll just get the address and get out of your hair.

DMITRI
You sure not stay for drinks, Jerry?

JERRY

DMITRI
C'mon Jerry, one shot for road.

JERRY
I don't really uh-

DMITRI
Don't make my mother cry Jerry, drink with me!

JERRY
Ah...... Fuck it.

DMITRI
Very good! 
(shouting)
MOTHER!

Dmitri's mom waddles into the room with a giant bottle of vodka in hand. Almost half as big as her.
